Domaine de la Taille aux Loups, a little jewel of the Loire!
Domaine de la Taille aux Loups was created in 1989 by Jacky Blot when he moved to Montlouis with his wife. After having some other jobs like Grand Crus trader, he decided to go for production of wines of a little known, at that time, appellation : the one called Montlouis. Then in 2002 he decided to extend to another grape variety, Cabernet Franc. He purchased then Domaine des Buttes in Bourgueil. As a strong supporter of sustainable wine production, he decided to grow his vines limiting chemical treatments and applying fragmented wine making. He was named « The Watchmaker of Montlouis » due to precision and rigor of his vintages !
One of the pioneers of sustainable agriculture
At the head of Domaine de la Taille aux Loups since 1989, Jacky Blot quickly made a step forward towards environmentally friendly agriculture, respectful of the labor. Yet at that time only a few vine growers made this choice, which is quite surprising. Nowadays, he's not alone but stands out from the crowd with high quality of his products, renowned by the biggest experts and guides (FYI, in 2016 he got a 5th star of Bettane et Desseauve guide like other iconic wine estates). Located on the territory of Montlouis-sur-Loire and Vouvray appellations, his estate also grows a unique grape variety - Chenin blanc, also called « le Pinot de la Loire ». Here the grapes are picked manually and the harvest starts as late as possible. For what concerns the wines, Jacky Blot is focused on dry, semi-dry, liqueur and dessert wines.
Wines of high standard
Over the years, this wine estate became a symbol of Montlouis. They currently produce a complete range of wines that you may find on our online shop. Among the essential references of Domaine de la Taille aux Loups, we may highlight Triple Zéro (sparkling wine), Le Clos de Mosny and Rémus Plus. As the yields of vines are limited for this wine property, the quantity of wine bottles is also limited. This explains the fact that on our website we only have a few references of this wine estate. So if you wish to discover these wines, try to avoid depletion of stocks !

Domaine de la Taille Aux Loups [Jacky & JP Blot]
Domaine de la Taille Aux Loups Jacky amp JP Blot
“With François Chidaine, Jacky Blot has been instrumental in taking Montlouis out of Vouvray’s shadow and establishing for it a reputation of its own—and a better one at that. Much of what he has done appears old hat today, but it was revolutionary at the time: organic viticulture, hand harvests, wild yeasts, barrel fermentations and no malolactic conversions” –Vinous Media
“Jacky’s wines, including his not-anymore Vouvray, are the perfect example: They’re bone-dry, less fruity than complex and austere. He believes sugar blurs chenin’s ability to transparently reveal its best qualities, which is why his winemaking is almost fanatically Burgundian, although he prefers to describe it as “the school of Montlouis.” He ferments all his whites in barrels. And rather than a cold, quick fermentation meant to highlight aromas, he borrows from Burgundy’s elite cadre, winemakers like Jean-François Coche (of Coche-Dury) and Jean-Marc Roulot (of Domaine Roulot): he exposes the grape must to oxygen before a long, slow fermentation and leaves the finished wine in steel tanks for months before bottling, which firms up the texture.” -Jon Bonné
The future of Loire Valley Chenin Blanc is in single vineyard, dry, terroir-driven whites that can compete with the best in the world for precision, length, complexity and ageability. The late, legendary Jacky Blot and his son Jean-Philippe understood this clearly and focused their domaine on making these crystalline Chenin from their organic sites in the best parts of the appellation. Ever since Jacky first purchased eight hectares of old vines in Montlouis in the late 1980s, he transformed and built up the domaine into one of the Loire’s finest addresses. The beautifully cared for sites are allowed to sing to their full potential, without sugar, without battonage, without malo, and minimal filtration. This domaine is without question one of the inspirational leaders of this growing movement towards world-class single site wines.

Domaine de la Taille aux Loups
Domaine de la Taille aux Loups is certainly one of the most significant domaines of Touraine and is, alongside the domaine of François Chidaine, an obvious candidate for appellation leader in Montlouis-sur-Loire. And yet this is a very young domaine, established only twenty-or-so years ago. For most of those years it was home to the late Jacky Blot (1948 – 2023), although it was not he who established it; frequently overlooked, the viticultural maverick who brought La Taille aux Loups into being was a man from Bordeaux named Christian Prudhomme.
Prudhomme clearly wanted to make waves in Montlouis-sur-Loire; having worked for the Rothschilds in the vineyards and cellars of Château Mouton-Rothschild, and also at Opus One in California, his curriculum vitae suggested he was up to the job. In 1988, having acquired 7 hectares of old vines scattered about the appellation, he set about making wine his way. This meant reducing yields by crop thinning, harvesting into tiny crates to protect the fruit and fermenting using indigenous yeasts, in barrels purchased from Château d’Yquem. The wines produced were reputedly a testament to the wild dedication he exhibited. So it seemed something of a vinous tragedy when the business collapsed within a year or two of starting up. But this is the point in which Jacky Blot (pictured) entered the story.

Jacky Blot, the vintner behind Domaine de la Taille Aux Loops, began his career in the wine trade as a courtier, a role in the wine business that is often overlooked. The position is a bit incognito, hidden between the château and the negociant, and acts as the catalyst between both sides of a business deal. They feed information to negociants on the general state of the château, and they report on who is performing well in the marketplace. This role requires a level of savvy and gave Jacky a strong intuitive understanding of the wine business that he often credits for his success today as a vintner. In 1989, Jacky purchased 20-acres in Montlouis-sur-Loire. Since then, he has tripled that area to include vineyards in Vouvray and Bourgueil. New on the scene and without any family reputation to spoil, Jacky showed zero reservations about causing a few waves in the local community with his approach to viticulture and winemaking. "Outrageous" techniques such as organic viticulture, plowing rather than using herbicides, not fertilizing the vines, spontaneous fermentations and, most scurrilous of all, barrel fermentation and barrel ageing, were the cause of many hard looks from his neighbors. But today Jacky has proved that his commitment to his philosophy has paid off, and his wines are some of the most exciting and trail-blazing of the region.
In 2010, he bought Clos de Mosny, 30-acre walled vineyard which is now his largest monopole in the Loire. It is planted to old Chenin vines of various ages and various clones that thrive in clay and flint soils. His Rémus is made from a second, slightly later harvest through this vineyard from 50 to 80-year-old vines that are low-yielding but produce highly concentrated berries. Spontaneous fermentation takes place in barrels in his cool underground cellar with absolutely no intervention, so fermentation is very slow, taking anywhere from four to nine months. The wine does not undergo malolactic fermentation, there is no barrel stirring, and there are no added sulfites during élevage - this is truly a hands-off, holistic wine! It then spends twelve months in barrel, of which only a judicious 20% is new. The resulting wine has an incredibly fresh nose with notes of melon, pear, citrus, and saline. The palate hits with a mouth-watering level of acidity driven by notes of lime zest and Meyer lemon. The bone-dry finish showcases a hint of creaminess and texture which elevates the wine to an experience beyond just a jolt of acidity and finishes with a nectarine sweetness that will convince you of the quality of this producer. Serve with a butter lettuce salad dressed in a lemon cream dressing for the perfect pairing!

Overview of the Wine  
A new star has emerged in the heart of the Loire Valley: he is Jacky Blot of Domaine de la Taille aux Loups, in Montlouis and Vouvray. Montlouis is located on the southern bank of the Loire, opposite Vouvray. Blot, originally a Loire wine broker by profession, acquired about 8 hectares of 50-75 year old vines in 1989. These prized, ancient parcels belonged to families that could no longer continue to cultivate the vines and so entrusted them to Blot and his team. Blot brought a passion and exacting determination to make wines of only the highest quality, well beyond the norm of the day. Now more than 25 years on, Blot is the acknowledged pioneer of the region and is credited with having taken Chenin Blanc to unprecedented heights of quality.

Winemaker's Tasting Notes  
From very old vines in Montlouis, this Chenin Blanc is incredibly complex, showing aromas and flavors of preserved Meyer lemon, white flowers, citrus rind, Anjou pear, and crushed rocks. Everything here is perfectly in balance, with a gorgeous lift to its mineral structural core. A long juicy finish rounds out this textural wonder.
94 Points - Vinous (2022 Vintage)The 2022 Montlouis-sur-Loire Les Hauts de Husseau hails from a site with vines between 80 and 110 years old. It's a finely scented, silken style that provides a mellow sense of effortlessness on the mid-palate before it structures itself toward the close. The chalky nature of the soil provides a fine coating of texture and structure, which adds persistence and line. It finishes long, calm, and focused, with notes redolent of pastry, ripe apple and chalky citrus.
